On December 31st, the customer contacted us and was quoted $700 for a full bee elimination with complex honeycomb removal from a roof cavity. This entailed performing a roof penetration to extract the hive which is the only method that includes a one-year warranty. The customer declined this option and stated they only wanted a kill. As they were selling the home and wanted to spend the least amount possible.

We clearly explained that a spray only treatment does not include a warranty and that without honeycomb removal, bee activity can return. The customer chose the $150 spray extermination option with no guarantee, fully understanding these limitations. This was not swarming bee but an established hive, likely containing 75+ pounds of honeycomb inside the structure, which significantly limits the effectiveness of spray-only treatments.

The spray service was performed on January 2nd.

On January 11th, the customer contacted us stating they were still seeing bees. On Monday morning January 12th we stated we would go out the next day to assess activity. Although the service was not under warranty, we returned on January 13th as a courtesy. During that visit, no live bee activity was observed, and video evidence of the property was taken and sent to the customer that same day.

After sending the video on January 13th, we did not receive any further communication from the customer until yesterday February 4th.

From the beginning and throughout the process, we consistently explained that without honeycomb removal, foraging and robber bees can continue to return. Spray treatments alone cannot reliably eliminate a hive of this size when honeycomb is layered within the structure.

We understand how stressful this can be when selling a home. We were transparent about pricing, limitations, and expectations from the start, and we returned outside of warranty as a courtesy. We remain willing to resolve the issue properly with the full complex honeycomb removal service at $700, which was the original recommendation.

Hi Madison,
Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. I completely understand how seeing existing weeds still standing can be frustrating, and I appreciate the opportunity to clarify the service we provided.

Our Weed Control Program is a professional chemical treatment, not a physical weed removal service. During your visit, we performed a full front and backyard treatment using both a post-emergent and pre-emergent application. The post-emergent is designed to kill the existing weeds at the root, and the pre-emergent works to prevent new weeds from growing for up to six months.

With spray treatments, weeds do not disappear immediately. Larger or mature weeds typically die back over several days to weeks, at which point they can be removed easily or will naturally break down. Pulling or cutting weeds at the time of treatment can actually reduce the effectiveness of the product, which is why it is not part of the service.

The 6-month guarantee refers to weed control and prevention meaning if weeds return during that time, we come back and retreat the affected areas at no additional charge. Manual removal has never been included in this service, but we understand how expectations can differ, and we are always happy to explain this more clearly going forward.

That said, we want you to feel confident in the service you received. If you notice weeds that are not responding to the treatment after the proper time frame, please reach out and we will gladly schedule a follow-up under your guarantee.

We truly appreciate your business and the chance to clarify. 

Best regards,
Magic Pest Control

You do have to be diligent and look for them in the folds and creases of furniture and the same for your mattress or mattress protector. I have pillow protectors too and found a couple hiding in the folds of the zippers. This product is called Crossfire and you can get it in spray which has to be mixed or in a can like WD40 with a straw attachment which works really well on baseboards and cracks. I bought another product called Harris and this spray came premixed, shake it up and use it. It had the same ingredients as Crossfire but a few dollars cheaper and I didn’t have to mix it. If you have a massive infestation, you definitely have to call the pros, but not Sexton. Disappointing service. reviews_data.review_text:
We hired Truly Nolan to remove roof rats from our property. The inspector/sales rep they sent over was very helpful, courteous, and knowledgeable. The inspector noticed a section of our overhang roofing that seemed to have a 1” gap running along it. He explained taking care of any existing rats would not be a problem, but we would need exclusion meshing to stop any new rats from getting in. All this made sense, inspired customer confidence, so we signed up.

The technicians that showed up were all very courteous to us, but a common trend was that they would voice their complaints about the company and the other technicians to us. One technician often showed up with a trainee shadowing them. We wondered if this constant presence of new trainees was due to expanding coverage in the valley, or a sign of high turnover. The technician training the new employee often coached them to leave lots of detailed notes, so the next tech would be prepared for the following visit. Then, the tech that showed up in the coming weeks would ask a number of rudimentary questions and explain no one had left much information on our account. Peculiar.

The exclusion mesh was often another topic the technicians complained about. The biggest issue is that they didn’t have any mesh. They would say that the previous technician didn’t indicate that we still needed it, or that the office was out. Ultimately, one of the technicians did show up and said, “I got this!” and held up a package of super fine 00000 steel wool. They packed the gap with sealant, filled it with fluffed up steel wool fibers, and packed in more sealant. It looks peculiar, but I am glad it’s hidden by the overhang of the roof.

Another issue was sanitation. The sales rep explained that once their techs had excluded the roof, they would come back in a few weeks to see if there was any rodent activity. If there wasn’t any activity, they would sanitize the attic. The sales rep noted that sanitation is important, and since the attic is large, cramped, and has lots of nooks and crevices, they use a chemical to fill the attic for sanitation. I am not sure if it’s a gas or a spray or what, but the sales rep explained it is harmless after an hour, but recommended we leave the house for 2 hours to allow it to harmlessly dissipate.

But this never happened. When the technician sealed the attic, they were done and left their equipment here. I contacted Truly Nolan, but didn’t receive a response. A few days ago I received a letter asking if I wanted to renew my contract. I called, and the receptionist was very kind. They noted that a tech indicated that the sanitation had occurred, but “perhaps they made a mistake, or marked off the service for the wrong account.” I also asked what exclusion mesh looks like, and they explained it was often a “thicker, chicken wire-type screen.” They said they could have a manager contact me in 1-2 business days.

To their credit, a manager reached out the next morning, but they lacked the courtesy we had encountered previously They seemed bewildered, defended their record of service, and said they would note that we did not want to renew our contract. They also said that the sanitation is immediate and does not require us to leave the house. This contradicted everything else we were told.

Aside from that representative, everyone at Truly Nolan was kind. People make mistakes, but as a company, I think you shouldn’t be afraid to own part of the problem and work to make things right. Honestly, I think about how they had so much trouble getting exclusion mesh, or the lack of notes. Perhaps, just like the exclusion mesh, the company could not secure the sanitation chemicals they were contracted to use. In looking at all the other reviews for Truly Nolan, you can see they are very careful of their brand name. All these 5 stars reviews make sure to name the technicians, and they are very quick to respond to any reviews below 5 stars. I do wish instead of spending that energy on protecting their image, they invested it in supporting their technicians in the field.
